newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan official says hostage prospects worsening.
newsitem.headline: Japan official says hostage prospects worsening.

text.p: The prospects of winning the release of high-level hostages in Peru are now worse than at any time since the seizure of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima last month, a Japanese government spokesman said on Saturday.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Hiroshi Hashimoto said at a news briefing that with no talks taking place between the government and the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement, "the situation is more serious than ever before."
"Dialogue began before the new year between the MRTA and the Peruvian government but now it has reached an impasse," he said.
Earlier on Saturday, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said he was "not optimistic" about ending the standoff.
"I am not optimistic about the situation, seeing as the number of hostages has been reduced to a level where it is easy for the terrorists to control them," Hashimoto told reporters.

The revolutionary group now has 74 hostages, after releasing an estimated 430 captives in several waves. They stormed the residence on December 17 during a party celebrating the birthday of Japan's emperor.
